item.title: Integrative Conceptual Reviews
item.content:encoded:
The Journal of Applied Psychology editorial team invites prospectus submissions that describe a proposed integrative conceptual review (ICR) manuscript on topic areas relevant to human resource management, industrial and organizational psychology, and organizational behavior.

An ICR article should be designed to synthesize relevant literature, identify significant knowledge gaps, highlight potential synergies between disconnected lines of research, extend theoretical development, and propose new directions for research.

Examples of the type of papers that are of interest include articles published in the Annual Review of Psychology, Psychological Science in the Public Interest, the Journal of Management review issue, the Academy of Management Annals, and top-tier handbooks.

Appel publié par Journal of Applied Psychology. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Human resource management
  • Industrial and organizational psychology
  • Organizational behavior
  • Literature synthesis and knowledge gap identification
  • Theoretical development and extension
  • New research directions

  • Invalid DateTime: ICR prospectus submission deadline
  • February 18, 2027: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Human-AI Interaction in Intelligent Workplaces: Behaviour, Trust, Experience, and Human-Centered Design
item.content:encoded:
Muhammad Imran Rasheed, University of Surrey

Barbara Rita Barricelli, Università degli Studi di Brescia

Waseem Ul Hameed, Universiti Utara Malaysia

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence systems are transforming workplace interactions, employee behavior, and organizational dynamics. While prior research has focused on AI adoption and performance outcomes, this collection addresses the human-centered dimensions of AI at work, including how employees develop trust in intelligent systems, experience AI-mediated processes, adapt their behaviors, and navigate issues such as technostress, autonomy, and cognitive load.

The special issue prioritizes behavioral, cognitive, and psychological perspectives on human-AI interaction in organizational settings. It seeks contributions that explore employee experiences with intelligent technologies, design of user-centered AI systems, transparency mechanisms, and the creation of psychologically sustainable digital work environments. The collection welcomes empirical, theoretical, and design-oriented research across quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method approaches.

item.title: Thirty Years of Affective Events Theory: New Directions in the Knowledge Era
item.content:encoded:
Rita Rueff-Lopes, Esade, Universitat Ramon Llull

Russell Cropanzano, Leeds School of Business, University of Colorado

José Navarro, Universitat de Barcelona

Ana Junça-Silva, ISCTE—Lisbon University Institute

This special issue revisits Affective Events Theory three decades after its original formulation, examining how it applies to contemporary work environments characterized by digitalization, datafication, and AI-mediated interactions. The issue seeks to extend AET's core propositions to explain how employees experience and respond to affective micro-events in modern organizational contexts, incorporating theoretical advancements and methodological innovations developed over the past 30 years.

The special issue welcomes original empirical research, theoretical contributions, and review articles that advance AET's boundaries across diverse contexts. Contributions should engage with emerging themes such as digital and hybrid work, multilevel dynamics of emotions, knowledge-intensive work environments, cross-cultural perspectives, and novel methodological approaches including experience sampling and emotion sensing technologies. Scholars are encouraged to challenge AET's assumptions, extend its mechanisms, and explore how affective processes operate within complex socio-technical work landscapes.

Appel publié par European Journal of Work and Organizational Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Revisiting the structure and boundaries of AET in digital, hybrid, and AI-augmented work contexts
  • Temporal, multilevel, and dynamic modeling of affective events in teams and organizations
  • Affective events in knowledge-intensive work, professional services, and virtual collaboration
  • Cross-cultural and individual differences in affective experience
  • Methodological advances such as experience sampling, multimodal emotion sensing, and computational text or voice analysis
  • Links between affective events and creativity, performance, well-being, and sustainability
  • Integrations with adjacent theories including emotion regulation, relational energy, job crafting, and affective climate
